rationale: Fresh three-lens re-review of the completed diff, superseding the stale round-1 request-changes. Both previously-raised blockers are confirmed resolved: a shared _sanitize_cell helper now routes through _build_csv and _build_xlsx to coerce non-primitive cells and strip openpyxl-illegal control chars (former CR-001) and to neutralize leading =,+,-,@,\t,\r formula-injection (former CR-002), each backed by regression tests (test_non_primitive_cells_are_stringified, test_illegal_control_chars_stripped, test_native_numeric_cells_preserved, test_xlsx/csv_neutralizes_formula_injection). Acceptance lens: every in-scope criterion passes; 3 items are na by design (openpyxl direct-dep promotion reverted per spec, in-chat download flow verified separately, suite not executed in review). No blocking findings survived triage. 4 dismissed (incl. a blind-lens false-positive 'missing type annotation' the real source has as file_repository: Optional[Any]; a backslash path-traversal concern that is non-exploitable because the storage backend assigns its own id and filename is display metadata; an unconfirmed empty-columns crash; and a None-masks-storage-error item that is pre-existing behavior of the reused FileExportService and matches the documented contract). 4 deferred as non-blocking edge cases on exotic input: lone UTF-16 surrogates not stripped by _sanitize_cell (crash on serialize); sheet titles not run through control-char sanitization (asymmetric with cells); case-insensitive sheet-name dedup ('Sales'/'sales') risking an Excel repair prompt; and no 32,767-char cell-length cap.
